access_intro: Nowhere is committed to making our app accessible to everyone, regardless of ability or technology. We believe in inclusive navigation and continuously work to improve the accessibility of our apps for people with disabilities.
access_statement_p: This accessibility statement applies to the Nowhere app. We aim to make Nowhere as accessible as we can, recognising that accessible technology supports all of us. Our goal is to enable everyone to navigate their world freely.
access_standards_p: We strive to align with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA, wherever reasonably practicable. These guidelines help us make digital content more accessible for people with disabilities and more usable for everyone.
access_doing_p: We are continuously reviewing our app design, navigation flows, colour contrast, font sizes and touch targets to improve accessibility. This includes support for screen readers, adjustable text sizes and sufficient colour contrast for people with low vision.
access_status_p: Nowhere is an open-source project built on community data. While we work towards full WCAG 2.1 AA conformance, some areas may not yet be fully accessible due to the nature of mobile maps and user-generated data. We are committed to improving these areas over time.
access_report_p: If you find any part of the Nowhere app difficult to use or access, or if you have ideas on how we could improve, please contact us. We take accessibility feedback seriously and will review every report.
access_feedback_p1: You can reach us via GitHub (
access_feedback_p3: , or email the address listed in the app. We normally respond to accessibility feedback within a few days.

privacy_p_overview: Nowhere is an open-source Android app that uses Android's mock location feature to simulate GPS positions on your device. We do not require an account and do not collect, store, or sell personal data. The app contains no analytics, advertising, or tracking SDKs.The app retrieves in-app announcements from a backend service (Supabase) and receives over-the-air updates via Expo (EAS Update). Both are described in Section 3. Neither involves an account, and we do not send any personal data or user identifiers to them.
privacy_p_device_data: The following data is stored only locally on your device (via Android's AsyncStorage) and is never transmitted to us:
privacy_li_device_1: App settings (movement mode, speeds, units, map style, language, joystick side)
privacy_li_device_3: Your favorite places and recently used places (coordinates and labels)
privacy_p_device_data_delete: You can delete this data at any time by clearing the app's data in your Android system settings or by uninstalling the app.
privacy_p_third_party: To provide its features, the app sends requests directly from your device to the following third-party services. We do not receive or process this data. As with any internet request, these services can see your IP address and device/request metadata.
privacy_p_routing: When you calculate a route, the coordinates of your start, stops, and destination are sent to public OSRM servers (routing.openstreetmap.de, with router.project-osrm.org as a fallback).
privacy_p_reverse: To show a readable address instead of raw coordinates, the app sends your current (simulated) position to the Nominatim service operated by the OpenStreetMap Foundation.
privacy_p_traffic_prefix: If you use the "traffic" speed mode, the app requests traffic signals and speed limits for the area around your route. The bounding box of your route is sent to Overpass API servers:
privacy_p_map_tiles: To display the map, the app loads map data. These requests reveal the map area you are viewing.
privacy_p_announcements: The app can show announcements (pop-ups), for example about new features or important changes. To do this, the app fetches a public announcements table from Supabase. The same announcements are shown to all users; they are not targeted at individuals. The request contains no account, device ID, or other user identifier. Whether you have seen an announcement is stored only on your device (see Section 2) and is not sent to us or to Supabase. Supabase, as our hosting provider, may process technical request data such as your IP address in its server logs. We do not use this data to identify you.
privacy_p_updates: The app can receive over-the-air (OTA) updates of its code and assets via EAS Update, provided by Expo. When the app checks for or downloads an update, your device sends technical request data to Expo's servers, such as the app's runtime version, platform, current update ID, and your IP address. This is required to deliver the correct update. We do not receive personal data through this process.
privacy_p_providers: These providers have their own privacy policies:
privacy_li_further_providers: Further providers: please consult their respective websites.
privacy_p_location: The app requires you to select it as the "mock location app" in Android's developer options. It uses this to provide simulated coordinates to other apps on your device. Simulated coordinates are only sent to the services listed above as described in Section 3.
privacy_p_sharing: We do not share, sell, or rent any personal data. Locally stored data remains on your device until you delete it. Data processed by third-party providers is subject to their respective retention policies.
privacy_p_children: The app is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect data from children.
privacy_p_rights: Since we do not collect or process personal data, there is no data about you for us to access, correct, or delete. If you are in the EU/EEA, you have rights under the GDPR with respect to the third-party providers above and can contact them directly.
